record.paper_title: Geometric and Topological Obstructions to Various Immersions in Submanifold Theory and Some Related Open Problems
record.context_brief: Finite- or low-type Gauss map obstructions
record.original_question: For a Riemannian manifold M of dimension at least 2, what conditions obstruct the existence of an isometric immersion of M into Euclidean space whose Gauss map is of finite type or low type? The Gauss map sends each point p of an immersed submanifold to the oriented normal subspace at p, represented as a point of the appropriate Grassmann manifold inside a Euclidean exterior-power space; finite type for such a map means decomposition into finitely many Laplacian eigenmap components.

evidence.quote: the classical Gauss map nu-hat can be defined as the map nu-hat : M -> G(m, m-n), n = dim M, which carries a point p in M to the linear (m-n)-subspace of E^m obtained from the normal space
Problem 7.9. What are the obstructions to isometric immersions of a Riemannian manifold into a Euclidean space with finite type (or low type) Gauss map?
it is interesting to obtain further obstructions for a submanifold in a Euclidean space with low type Gauss map.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a connected Riemannian manifold of dimension $n \geq 2$, and consider isometric immersions $f: M \to \mathbb{E}^m$ of $M$ into Euclidean $m$-space. The classical Gauss map of such an immersion is the map
$$\hat{\nu}: M \to G(m, m-n),$$
sending each point $p \in M$ to the oriented $(m-n)$-dimensional normal subspace of $f(M)$ at $f(p)$, where $G(m, m-n)$ denotes the Grassmannian of oriented $(m-n)$-planes in $\mathbb{E}^m$, viewed (via the Plücker embedding) as a compact submanifold of the Euclidean exterior-power space $\Lambda^{m-n}\mathbb{E}^m \cong \mathbb{E}^N$.

A smooth map $\phi: M \to \mathbb{E}^N$ from a Riemannian manifold $M$ is said to be of finite type if it admits a finite spectral decomposition
$$\phi = \phi_0 + \phi_1 + \phi_2 + \cdots + \phi_k,$$
where $\phi_0$ is a constant vector and $\phi_1, \dots, \phi_k$ are non-constant $\mathbb{E}^N$-valued maps satisfying $\Delta \phi_i = \lambda_i \phi_i$ for distinct eigenvalues $\lambda_1, \dots, \lambda_k$ of the Laplace–Beltrami operator $\Delta$ of $M$. The map is called of $k$-type, and is said to be of low type if $k$ is small (typically $k \in \{1, 2\}$).

Determine necessary geometric and topological conditions on $M$ (for instance, conditions on its curvature invariants, topology, or completeness) that obstruct the existence of an isometric immersion $f: M \to \mathbb{E}^m$ (for any $m \geq n$) such that the Gauss map $\hat{\nu}: M \to G(m, m-n) \subset \mathbb{E}^N$ is of finite type, respectively of low type.
artifact.status_search_result: The general problem of characterizing obstructions to isometric immersions of Riemannian manifolds into Euclidean space whose Gauss map is of finite or low type is posed as an open problem in surveys of finite-type submanifold theory. While many partial classification results exist for specific classes (surfaces, hypersurfaces, ruled submanifolds, tubes, etc.) with 1-type or 2-type Gauss maps, no general obstruction theory is known. Recent work continues to extend partial results case-by-case rather than resolving the general question.

status_evidence.title: Riemannian Submanifolds: A Survey (Chen)
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of finite-type submanifolds and finite-type Gauss maps with many open problems regarding low-type Gauss map characterizations.
status_evidence.claim: The general problem of obstructions for finite/low-type Gauss maps is listed among open problems in finite-type submanifold theory.

status_evidence.title: The Gauss map of immersions of Riemannian manifolds in spaces of constant curvature
status_evidence.snippet: Classical study of Gauss maps for isometric immersions; results are partial and class-specific.
status_evidence.claim: Existing obstructions are of partial nature and apply to restricted classes of submanifolds.
